# area: overloads
# hypothesis: Literal and union arguments select the matching overload, and the runtime branch returned matches the literal-selected overload.
from typing import Literal, TypeVar, assert_type, overload, reveal_type

T = TypeVar('T')


@overload
def pick(flag: Literal[True]) -> int: ...
@overload
def pick(flag: Literal[False]) -> str: ...
@overload
def pick(flag: bool) -> int | str: ...
def pick(flag: bool) -> int | str:
    return 1 if flag else 'no'


@overload
def first(items: list[T]) -> T: ...
@overload
def first(items: str) -> str: ...
def first(items: list[T] | str) -> T | str:
    return items[0]


a = pick(True)
assert_type(a, int)
b = pick(False)
assert_type(b, str)
flag: bool = len('ab') > 1
c = pick(flag)
reveal_type(c)
assert c == 1
assert_type(first([3, 4]), int)
assert first('xy') == 'x'
u: list[int] | str = [9] if flag else 'zz'
reveal_type(first(u))
assert first(u) == 9
pick('yes')  # expect-error
hypothesis: Literal and union arguments select the matching overload, and the runtime value returned matches the overload chosen for a literal argument.
